questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Meeting new people and living on my own in a new country

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy I got guided to my flat all the way from the station, and got the rest of my information on my student mail, from the abroad university.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I got guided on how to get to my flat.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: You could choose if you wanted shared toilet or nah.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There was a meal plan available but it is not worth it.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Super nice people you will most likely live with other exchange students from other countries.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Pretty easy you got mails on how to do online registretion, and how to wish housing and stuff.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: All information I got through mail.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Really succesful i even regretted one of my courses during weak 1 and they easily switched me over to another course.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
If you are a semester 1 only student like me, they will most likely scare you by saying you will be forced to take exams, in May-June, because that is the ordinary exam time, but atleast for me and all the other exchange students i talked to, they just changed the course to instead give us specificly a test in the last week, that will work as our exam, so dont worry about the ordinary exam for a lot of courses being in May-June.
In general they are super large when it comes to that kind of stuff.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: All my courses were honor levels which corrosponds to about 3rd year courses in denmark.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching is a lot less person to person, there is not practice lessons in smaller groups with a TA, instead there is tutorials which is kind of a lecture, where one of the TA's go through some of the exercises and explain how they are solved.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
LH Machine Learning,
LH Intelligent Robotics,
LH Security of Real-World Systems

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I took LH Machine learning as a replacement for Machine Learning A at the University of Copenhagen, it was very much what you would expect a very theory based look at Machine Learning.
LH Intelligent Robotics is pretty interesting and also coursework only where you make a project during the course.
LH Security of Real-World Systems was my most favorite course super interesting and a very interesting way to learn security. Our assignments was completing quest in a video game, where we had to use the skills, we learned in the lectures, to tamper with the game. Just a extremely nice made course. The final exam for us semester 1 students, was also super large, we were given 2 days to complete a exam set, that normally you would have 2 hours in a sit down exam. Super nice course take it if you are interested in security the slightest.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
We are already given bedding, duvet and pillow, and we are already given cutlery, a small plate, a big plate and a 
deep plate. You are also given pots and pans to share on the flat, so a lot of these kinds of things you dont have to worry about.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is a insane amount of socities, and i would recommend to try and join the socity fairs and sport fairs in the first couple of days, and try and go to as many tasters as possible to meet a lot of new people.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I loved to travel with my flatmates, around the UK but also Ireland, or even other places in europe.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel around and make sure you have something planned for every weekend.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join as many tasters, and talk to your flatmates those were the people i hanged out with the most.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I found most groceries a lot more cheap than in denmark.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Dont worry about exams being in May-June they are super large and it will work out no matter how much they scare you with sending forms.
Make sure you are quickly to rent a room when you get the opportunity, you will be told that semster 1 only students are not guaranteed a room, but as long as your not too slow im pretty sure you are pretty much guaranteed.
Try as many tasters from different sports and socities.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The same as important thing

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Challenging your boundories, and meeting new people.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I dont know

Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
